title: Console Pathfinder: Compact Navigation & Workspace Handoff
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: As teams adopt Redwood Dedicated and Private instances, power users need faster lateral moves across projects, routes, and environments without losing task context. Current console navigation is optimized for discoverability but forces full-page context switches and long path hunts for rollouts, cost breakdowns, and route-level dashboards. Goal: design a compact, context-preserving navigation pivot (the 'Pathfinder') that surfaces high-frequency destinations (dashboards, rollouts, cost views) and enables frictionless workspace handoff across teammates while preserving discoverability for new users. Success metrics: reduce average time-to-target for common flows (Open rollout > details, Open cost view, Jump to embedding route) by 30%, and reduce cross-workspace switch errors by 40% in usability tests.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Pathfinder present on left edge as a collapsed micro-rail and expands on hover/click; 2) Quick-actions (open rollout, open cost breakdown, open trace) available inline with keyboard shortcuts; 3) Workspace handoff flow allows attaching current route + transient view (filters/state) to a shareable link and selecting teammate to notify; 4) Accessibility: full keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels for all controls; 5) Prototype validated with 8 product/eng/design participants with improvements logged and no critical usability blockers.
tradeoffs_and_decisions:
- Chose a micro-rail over a full-width persistent sidebar to keep primary content real estate for dashboards.
- Decided against pre-populating the rail with all routes to avoid cognitive overload; instead we show pinned + recent + suggested by usage heuristics.
- Workspace handoff is implemented as a lightweight share + notify pattern rather than making it a full collaboration layer (scope, timeline).
- Deferred per-team custom shortcuts to a follow-up EPIC to avoid blocking initial rollout.
activity: 2025-02-19 - Kickoff with PM (Lena Ortiz) and Eng Lead (Ravi Patel). Confirmed metrics and scope: rollouts, cost, traces prioritized.
2025-02-21 - Early sketch review: two patterns (stacked micro-rail vs. floating palette). Design team leaned to micro-rail for predictability.
2025-02-25 - Proto v1 created in Figma. Includes collapsed state, hover reveal, pinned/recent sections, and quick-action menu. Shared with Eng for feasibility.

2025-02-27 - Eng feasibility sync (ENG-4892): KV cache update and route-prefetch required for sub-second jumps. Eng flagged a potential perf spike for very large orgs; added as dependency to implement batched prefetch and lazy-load icons.
2025-02-28 - Usability session 1 (internal): 6 participants. Findings: users liked quick-actions, some confusion around 'handoff' wording; recommended rename to 'Send view'.
2025-03-01 - Updated prototype: replaced 'Handoff' label, added confirmation microcopy, added keyboard shortcut mapping. Added accessibility notes for aria-expanded/aria-controls.
2025-03-02 - PM review: asked to include a lightweight telemetry plan to track time-to-target and share usage. Linked to PM analytics ticket PM-2647.
2025-03-03 - Design critique: accepted with minor changes. Preparing final spec and handoff to Eng for spike and implementation plan. Assigned follow-ups for localization copy and e2e test cases.
open_questions: Should suggested items on the rail be personalized per user or per workspace? (Product trade-off: relevance vs. predictable shared navigation)
What is the acceptable TTL for the transient 'Send view' links? (24h vs 7d vs indefinite)
Do we provide a global toggle to revert to full legacy sidebar for admins during rollout?
next_steps: 1) Finalize telemetry spec with PM and Analytics (PM-2647). 2) Eng spike to prototype route-prefetch and icon lazy-loading (ENG-4892). 3) Localize microcopy and add i18n keys. 4) Schedule 2nd round of usability tests (external pilot customers) and collect time-to-target metrics. 5) Hand off final Figma frames + redlines to eng and create implementation tickets.
notes_for_engineering:
- Prefetch should use batched route metadata endpoints and respect rate limits to avoid cold-start spikes.
- Provide an opt-in to disable heuristics for orgs with strict visibility controls.
- Minimal backend support: endpoint to generate time-limited 'Send view' token and an event webhook for notifications.
- Route transitions should not reload the entire SPA if the destination is within the same app shell; use internal route state restore to preserve dashboard filters.
